Definition: to dig; by analogy, to engrave; figuratively, to explain
BiblicalUsage: Ba'ar means to dig, to make plain — to engrave words so clearly that a runner can read them. Moses was charged to write the law plainly on stones, and Habakkuk was told to write the vision and make it plain upon tables, that he may run that readeth it.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God wants his word plain — written large on stone, written clear on the tablet — because he wants runners, not scholars, to carry it. That is why I write plainly too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
